```{r setup, include = FALSE}
knitr::opts_chunk$set(collapse = TRUE, comment = "#>")
```

```{r}
library(RcmdrShiny)
```

# Overview

The Data Studio is the **Data** tab in Studio mode. It turns the historical
view/edit pane into a complete data preparation workspace while keeping the
engine rule unchanged: any change that modifies the data is an R command.

This vignette walks through the lifecycle **import -> inspect -> clean ->
derive -> export**.

# A small data set

For the examples we use a data frame created in a private environment, the
same way the tests do:

```{r}
env <- new.env()
env$Dataset <- data.frame(
  id = 1:6,
  group = factor(rep(c("a", "b"), 3)),
  score = c(10, 12, 11, 15, 14, 16),
  weight = c(1.2, 1.4, 1.1, 1.8, 1.6, 1.9)
)
state <- AppState(env = env)
active_dataset(state, "Dataset")
```

The data set registry lists it with its dimensions and classes:

```{r}
RcmdrShiny:::dataset_registry(state)
```

# Inspect a column

`RcmdrShiny:::column_profile()` is the same function behind the inspector:

```{r}
profile <- RcmdrShiny:::column_profile(state, "Dataset", "score")
profile$type
profile$stats
profile$levels
```

Numeric profiles include a compact histogram, factor and character profiles
include level counts.

# Clean with commands

Structural operations are generated as commands. Here we add a computed
column, then remove it again:

```{r}
command <- RcmdrShiny:::cmd_add_column("Dataset", "ratio", expression = "score / weight")
command
run_command(state, command)
env$Dataset$ratio
```

Deleting the column is another command:

```{r}
run_command(state, RcmdrShiny:::cmd_delete_columns("Dataset", "ratio"))
names(env$Dataset)
```

# Select and subset

Row selection is a session state. It is translated into a reproducible
subset command only when you ask for it:

```{r}
RcmdrShiny:::set_data_selection(state, rows = c(1L, 3L), columns = c("id", "score"))
RcmdrShiny:::selection_summary(state)
sub <- RcmdrShiny:::selection_subset_command(state, "DatasetSubset")
sub
run_command(state, sub)
env$DatasetSubset
```

A filtered view is different: it never changes the data set and never adds a
command to the log.

# Checkpoints

Before a destructive operation the Data Studio creates a checkpoint:

```{r}
checkpoint <- RcmdrShiny:::checkpoint_create(state, "Before deleting rows")
run_command(state, RcmdrShiny:::cmd_delete_rows("Dataset", c(1, 2)))
nrow(env$Dataset)
RcmdrShiny:::checkpoint_restore(state, checkpoint$id)
nrow(env$Dataset)
```

A restore is a session operation. It is noted in the structured history but
does not add a command to the script.

# Data dictionary

Labels and units are stored as attributes:

```{r}
RcmdrShiny:::set_variable_label(state, "Dataset", "score", label = "Score", units = "points")
RcmdrShiny:::variable_label(state, "Dataset", "score")
attr(env$Dataset$score, "label", exact = TRUE)
```

The same values are exported by the dictionary table:

```{r}
RcmdrShiny:::dictionary_table(state, "Dataset")
```

# Import preview

`RcmdrShiny:::preview_import_file()` reads the first rows, detects the delimiter and
proposes column types. The wizard uses it to show the preview before it
generates the `read.table()` command.

```{r, eval = FALSE}
RcmdrShiny:::preview_import_file("data.csv", header = TRUE)
```

# Export

Exporting is a command like any other:

```{r, eval = FALSE}
run_command(state, RcmdrShiny:::cmd_export_data("Dataset", "dataset.csv"))
```

The toolbar also exposes the download buttons for CSV and `.RData`.

# Design notes

- The grid is a view; it never becomes a second editing engine.
- Every structural change goes through `run_command()`, so it appears in the
  script, the output and the structured history.
- Checkpoints are capped by count and memory; large data sets fall back to
  targeted actions instead of disabling the workspace.
- The Data Studio adds no statistical procedure: it reuses the existing
  dialogs and command builders.
